    Dwarves¶

    One of the Six Main Races of Ge'or — a sturdy, long-lived humanoid species that once dominated the world through industry. Dwarves are the master craftsmen of Ge'or: brilliant smiths, miners, and mass producers whose works are found in every nation. Their golden age was Age 5, when underground megacities fueled by Romanium ore supplied the entire known world.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: 150–170 cm tall, stocky and broad-shouldered. Males grow huge beards — a point of pride and identity. Hypermasculine bearing regardless of actual gender
    • Lifespan: Up to 200 years. Dwarves reproduce late — typically at 90–100 years of age
    • Mage-cell expression: Low. Dwarves favor craft and steel over spells
    • Traits: Exceptional endurance. Precision and perfectionism in everything they build. Their constitution shrugs off hardship that would break other species

    Society¶

    Dwarven society is honor-bound, proud, and industrious — built around craft, clan, and community.

    • Governance: Clan-based monarchies and guild-councils. Dwarven nations include Dwarvengor, Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, and the Purple Coast
    • Culture: Honorable, prideful, and fiercely loyal, with a great sense of humor — and heavy drinking. Industry is identity: mass production in a medieval world, where precision is a form of worship
    • Religion: Dwarvism — the Three Doctrines (Coal, Diamond, and Emerald)
    • Relations: Rivalry with Elves — a healthy, respectful opposition of industry vs. nature. Treasured trade partners with Humans. Mixed communities exist in Dwarvengor and the mountain cities of East Erisdar
    • Weakness: A high death rate — mining accidents, industrial hazards, and combat glory claim many dwarves before their time
    • Subgroups: Eastern Dwarves — surface-dwelling, trade-oriented, cosmopolitan

    History¶

    • Age 5 — Dwarf Era (−5,499 to −4,500 BGD) — Dwarves dominated Ge'or through underground megacities fueled by Romanium ore. They manufactured weapons, tools, and commodities for most of the known world.
    • Economic collapse — When Romanium ran out, the dwarven economy collapsed over centuries. The world entered Age 6.
    • Modern era — Dwarven presence persists strongly in nations like Dwarvengor, Coalsteel Kingdom, Diamonds Kingdom, Cobal Kingdom, and Purple Coast.
    • Subgroups — Eastern Dwarves (surface-dwelling, trade-oriented, cosmopolitan)
